# Reading Last Season's Numbers in Context

<sub>Proposed by the synthesis, not on the user's list.</sub>

**Summary.** Treat last season's stats as a starting point, not a price tag. Before the 2026-10-18 auction, cut back numbers built on injured teammates, tanking stretches, hot streaks and rested low-minute samples. Do not throw out a good player because of one bad or hidden season either. During the season, sell fill-in starters while they still look like starters, and well before the 2027-03-04 trade deadline.

## Start from last season, then adjust

Last season's line is the base. It is not the answer. Production follows minutes, role and opportunity, and all three can change over a summer. Take the past numbers, then adjust for teammates who arrived and teammates who left. Before you bid, play the prediction game. Write down a realistic stat line in our nine categories and ask whether it justifies the price you are about to pay. ([09-10](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=575), [09-01](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=407), [09-22](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=1057), [09-29](https://youtu.be/XSPJL_mlFXo?t=444))

Last season's rank still has a use. It shows how much a player must improve to earn his current cost. A player priced well above last season's finish needs a real reason to jump, like a bigger role or a returning teammate leaving. If you cannot name that reason, let someone else pay. ([09-22](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=1350), [07-14](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=980))

Myopia cuts both ways. Do not overpay for one good season. Do not write a player off after one bad season either. Stats from a tanking stretch, an injury or a minutes cap can hide a player's real value. Market prices tend to follow last season, so the players who look bad on last season's list are where the auction discounts are. Use last season's top and bottom lists as a baseline, not as a reason to buy or fade. Also ignore whether a player won or ruined your league last year. That season will not repeat. ([08-20](https://youtu.be/s28HvC2grAk?t=405), [10-02](https://youtu.be/ZYllcj4o6_A?t=2253), [09-09](https://youtu.be/7BllEsdNLoM?t=1194), [09-25](https://youtu.be/Bi1cEM03k9Y?t=600), [07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=2805), [09-28](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=1507))

The experts do not fully agree on how far back to look. Most of the notes say to check several seasons and the career range, for example when judging games played. One note says multi-year history does not predict better than last season alone. Both sides agree on one thing: do not draft straight off last season's rankings. The speaker who rejects ranking-only drafting warns that you miss the players worth jumping for and take crowd-avoided players too early. In practice, use the extra seasons to explain the context behind last year. Do not average them blindly. ([09-22](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=1165), [09-10](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=441), [07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=122), [08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1576), [07-20](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=284), [07-20](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=275))

## Games with teammates out

Big numbers posted while key teammates were injured are hard to repeat once those teammates come back. Scale them down. Be extra careful when the production came mainly while two or three teammates were out. Before you bid, check who was around the player, who was missing, and how the coach used him when the team was healthy. ([09-19](https://youtu.be/uarqbNA2dFk?t=240), [09-10](https://youtu.be/dlo7L8Ru91A?t=1145), [06-23](https://youtu.be/nnWX_ObljOE?t=324), [08-25](https://youtu.be/H9q2FT3LhNw?t=1400), [09-07](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=1742))

One note gives a hard anchor. A bench player who put up numbers in big injury minutes should be valued near his healthy-team role, around 150th, unless something changes. Our draft takes 144 players, so 150th sits just outside the drafted pool. That player is a 1 USD end-of-roster pick at most, or a waiver add. ([08-23](https://youtu.be/hm5-fiCa5S4?t=2216))

Scoring built on borrowed usage shrinks the most. Players who score big only when injuries push their usage up produce much less when asked to scale back. Off-court splits from when one star sat can also go stale. If the roster has since added other high-usage players, those splits do not fit the new situation. The same goes for position. Stats a wing piled up while playing center may not hold once he moves back to his normal spot on a healthy team. ([08-23](https://youtu.be/hm5-fiCa5S4?t=1689), [09-25](https://youtu.be/Bi1cEM03k9Y?t=295), [07-20](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=1656))

Shooting percentages depend on lineup context too. Playing next to stars who draw defenders creates open looks. Playing as the lone creator on a bench unit does not. In our league FG% and FT% are team ratios, and high-volume shooters move them most. So before you pay for a high-volume shooter, check which lineup his percentages came from. ([07-26](https://youtu.be/75Sk_4fkgIM?t=2054))

## Late-season tanking and post-deadline numbers

Big March and April numbers on tanking teams mean little. Everyone is out and the team is trying to lose. Late-season usage spikes often come in meaningless games. Backup stats from March and April are often not real, and they stop being trustworthy once the team adds players ahead of them. One expert is especially skeptical of late-season production from Sacramento. ([08-05](https://youtu.be/CI4k8ofUXXk?t=562), [09-10](https://youtu.be/dlo7L8Ru91A?t=1875), [08-18](https://youtu.be/FxaSnyk9g90?t=334), [06-23](https://youtu.be/9tb1ARBEmQU?t=923), [07-14](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=1232))

Late-season shooting is inflated twice over. Teammates sit, and so do players on the opposing teams. Discount late-season FG% and FT% before you count them toward our ratio categories. ([07-14](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=325))

Do not throw out every post-deadline number, though. Check each case: will the conditions behind the rise still exist this season? One expert starts second-half splits on the Monday after the trade deadline. That skips the chaotic stretch when traded players are moving and rosters are thin. And as noted above, a tanking stretch can understate a good player's value as well as inflate a backup's. ([07-14](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=898), [07-14](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=68), [09-09](https://youtu.be/7BllEsdNLoM?t=1194))

## Hot streaks and limited-minute samples

After an extreme hot stretch, such as a post All-Star run, use the earlier part of the season as the baseline. Expect the shooting to come down. Before trusting hot shooting from a stretch with teammates injured, look for a bigger sample of about 45 to 50 games. Watch for highlight-reel bias. A few early big games can create hype the full season does not support. Judge the player on his percentages and category output, not the story around him. ([08-25](https://youtu.be/H9q2FT3LhNw?t=601), [08-24](https://youtu.be/rnq3118kfhY?t=1682), [07-21](https://youtu.be/RyzcCGChYgs?t=274), [07-13](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=1215), [09-01](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=452))

When many players on one team had career years at once, expect some of them to regress, often together. Fans and media tend to treat a team-wide hot streak as the new normal. That is your cue not to pay for every player on that roster. ([08-23](https://youtu.be/hm5-fiCa5S4?t=226), [08-23](https://youtu.be/hm5-fiCa5S4?t=292))

Limited-minute samples need the same care. Strong numbers posted with lots of rest, such as no back-to-backs or playing every other game, should be scaled back. Games played can also overstate a healthy sample. Many of Jalen Williams' 40 games were limited-minute games while he recovered from injuries. The opposite trap also exists. Playing every game adds nothing if the per-game line would not be rostered in a 12-team league. ([08-17](https://youtu.be/LcZcvk8s1xQ?t=1835), [07-26](https://youtu.be/75Sk_4fkgIM?t=164), [09-19](https://youtu.be/uarqbNA2dFk?t=930))

In season, react correctly to streaks. Stats are volatile, and no player matches his averages every night. Do not drop proven players during a cold stretch. Do not spend FAB or one of your six weekly adds chasing a hot streak that will normalize. ([09-01](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1052), [09-01](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1847))

## Finals hangovers

Teams coming off a Finals run may have a hangover, and their players are unlikely to repeat last season's production. Players often start slow after a long championship run, with production dips and fatigue. Defending champions tend to rest players and trim starters' minutes early in the season. Teams coming off long playoff runs may stay careful with their main players' minutes. Before the auction, check which teams went deep last spring. Price their key players for fewer minutes in the first weeks, not for last season's full line. ([09-09](https://youtu.be/7BllEsdNLoM?t=1565), [08-11](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=1025), [08-19](https://youtu.be/J1Eg3uaAICU?t=1082), [08-13](https://youtu.be/okN3fbHJtlA?t=703), [09-14](https://youtu.be/LM0cRCGoAUQ?t=1532))

## When to sell a fill-in starter

When a player who is not a real starter puts up starter numbers, sell him right away. Those numbers will not get better. A player's best breakout chance is the season with the most opening. When the stars return, expect a step back, not growth. Once the injured starters are back, he goes back to a reserve role. ([07-05](https://youtu.be/4kKINkZhWls?t=3517), [07-30](https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8?t=1030), [07-01](https://youtu.be/W3THnI7wWdA?t=1319), [09-10](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=1494))

Sell before the team starts trying to win again, because those chances will not come back. In our league that means trading him while his recent lines still look like a starter's. Trades are common here and the deadline is 2027-03-04, so do not wait until the last week. Also be skeptical of preseason 'maybe he gets the minutes' stories. Opportunity spikes and shooting spikes often never happen, so do not pay up for them on 2026-10-18. ([08-05](https://youtu.be/CI4k8ofUXXk?t=587), [07-05](https://youtu.be/4kKINkZhWls?t=1437))
